title: Polynomial associated graded implies regularity in a Noetherian local ring
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring with $1\ne0$, meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal, and assume that $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $b\geq0$, let $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in\mathfrak m$, and put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ and $C=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Suppose that the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_J(A),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ is an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, with M=A; the quasi-regular hypothesis is expanded using Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence.

proof.text: Since every $f_j\in\mathfrak m$, we have $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $1\notin J$ and $C=A/J\ne0$. The Jacobson radical is $\mathfrak m$, since this is the unique maximal ideal. For $0\leq i\leq b$ put $I_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ and $B_i=A/I_i$; let $q_i:A\to B_i$ be the quotient map and put $\overline J_i=(q_i(f_{i+1}),\ldots,q_i(f_b))$. The module $B_i$ is finite over $A$: every class is $a\cdot q_i(1)$. Because $q_i(f_j)=0$ for $j\leq i$, the images of all the generators of $J$ generate precisely $\overline J_i$. Thus $J^nB_i=\overline J_i^{\,n}$ as additive subgroups of $B_i$ for every $n\geq0$: expand products of $n$ generators, with the case $n=0$ giving $B_i$. Also $B_i/\overline J_i=C$: both send a representative $a$ to its class modulo $J$.

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, setup and quotient stages of its induction; Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (2), Jacobson hypothesis.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-quasi-regular-prefix-quotient] to the assumed canonical graded isomorphism, for each $0\leq i<b$. It gives a canonical graded isomorphism
$$\Phi_i:C[T_{i+1},\ldots,T_b]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}_{\overline J_i}(B_i),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[q_i(f_j)]_1.$$
The coefficient identification and the prefix quotients are exactly those introduced in Step 1. No regularity of any prefix is assumed in this application.

source.place: Tags 061R, lemma-truncate-quasi-regular, and 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, last paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $0\leq i<b$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with ring $A$, ideal $J$, and finite $A$-module $B_i$. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is Noetherian, $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ is contained in its Jacobson radical, and $B_i$ is cyclic by Step 1. Hence $\bigcap_{n\geq0}J^nB_i=0$, equivalently $\bigcap_{n\geq0}\overline J_i^{\,n}=0$. For $x\ne0$ in $B_i$, choose the least $n$ such that $x\notin\overline J_i^{\,n}$. Since $\overline J_i^{\,0}=B_i$, we have $n\geq1$; writing $r=n-1$ gives $x\in\overline J_i^{\,r}\setminus\overline J_i^{\,r+1}$. Thus its initial class $\xi=[x]_r$ is nonzero in degree $r$ of the associated graded ring.

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, first paragraph; Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (2), which generalizes the cited Tag 00IP, lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero.

proof.text:
Let $P=\Phi_i^{-1}(\xi)$, a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $r$. Multiplication by the variable $T_{i+1}$ is injective even if $C$ has zero divisors: it sends each coefficient at exponent $\alpha$ to that at $\alpha+e_{i+1}$, and distinct exponents remain distinct. Hence $T_{i+1}P
e0$. The homogeneous multiplication formula gives
$$0
e\Phi_i(T_{i+1}P)=[q_i(f_{i+1})]_1\,[x]_r=[q_i(f_{i+1})x]_{r+1}.$$
Consequently $q_i(f_{i+1})x
e0$. Since this holds for every nonzero $x\in B_i$, multiplication by $f_{i+1}$ on $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ has zero kernel and is injective (apply the zero-kernel assertion to the difference of two elements with equal products).

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, nonzero initial-form argument; Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular, multiplication by a variable.

proof.text: Step 4 gives exactly the required injectivity on every successive quotient, for $i=0,\ldots,b-1$. Step 1 gives the remaining condition $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)=C\ne0$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] these conditions mean that $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ is an $A$-regular sequence. If $b=0$, there are no injectivity conditions, $J=0$, and the last condition is $A\ne0$, which is assumed; hence the same conclusion holds for the empty sequence.

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, conclusion using Tag 00LF, definition-regular-sequence; empty-sequence case made explicit.
